editorial.meta_description: ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) exam covers contract, company, and employment law for ACCA students seeking the qualification.
editorial.overview: ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) is a computer-based exam administered by ACCA. It tests knowledge of contract law, company law, and employment law across 100 questions in a linear format, with a 120-minute duration and a passing score of 50. Candidates sit the paper as part of the ACCA Qualification and combine objective test questions with constructed response items drawn from the three syllabus domains.
editorial.who_should_take: ACCA students working toward the ACCA Qualification who need to demonstrate legal knowledge. It suits early-stage candidates building the business-law grounding required for later papers and practical experience.
skills_summary: Apply contract law principles to business scenarios
Interpret company law and the Companies Act 2006
Analyse employment law obligations and rights
Distinguish legal rules across the three syllabus domains
Use objective test and constructed response formats
editorial.preparation_strategy: Work through the official syllabus chapter by chapter, pairing each topic with practice questions from an up-to-date revision kit. Use ACCA technical articles to deepen understanding of the Companies Act 2006, the Bribery Act 2010, and money laundering regulations. Time yourself on full mock exams to build speed across the 100 questions within 120 minutes.

domain_guidance.summary: Domain 1 covers contract law, the foundation for commercial transactions tested in LW/F4. Candidates learn how agreements are formed, performed, and enforced in business contexts, including remedies available when obligations are not met.
study_focus: Key differences between contract and tort of negligence

domain_guidance.summary: Domain 2 covers company law, with emphasis on the Companies Act 2006. Candidates study company formation, share capital, directors, and corporate governance as examinable under LW/F4, including statutory duties and shareholder rights.
study_focus: Types of companies and registration under CA 2006

domain_guidance.summary: Domain 3 covers employment law as it applies in the LW/F4 syllabus. Candidates examine the legal framework governing the employment relationship and statutory protections available to workers and employers under UK legislation.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared for a 120-minute linear computer-based exam with 100 questions. Manage your time across objective test questions and constructed response items, and confirm the passing score of 50 before you begin.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) exam contains 100 questions in total. These combine objective test questions (OTQ) and constructed response items within a linear computer-based format administered by ACCA.
The passing score for ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) is 50. Candidates must achieve at least this mark across the 100 questions to pass the exam and progress in the ACCA Qualification.
ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) runs for 120 minutes. Candidates must complete all 100 questions within this fixed duration in a linear format under standard ACCA exam conditions.

faq.question_title: How much does the exam cost?
faq.answer_text: The exam price for ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) is $202.00. Candidates should confirm current fees directly with ACCA when booking their session, as prices may change over time.

Yes, ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) requires renewal. Candidates should check with ACCA for the current certification path and ongoing membership requirements applicable to their student or affiliate status.

faq.question_title: What domains does the exam cover?
faq.answer_text: ACCA Corporate and Business Law (LW/F4) covers three domains: contract law, company law, and employment law. Each domain tests legal knowledge relevant to professional accountancy practice and the wider business environment.
